subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be unconditionally denied patch access to legacy session rows without a `pluginOwnerId`, or should authority be established through an explicit migration or operator action?
rationale: The security fix changes access to persistent rows reachable from released versions, and repository policy requires explicit intent rather than an implicit runtime compatibility rule.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Confirm that plugins have no authority over ownerless rows and require deployed upgrade proof showing operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

options.title: Migrate ownership explicitly
options.body: Add a doctor- or operator-owned migration that establishes authority before plugin-runtime patch access resumes.

options.title: Defer ownerless-row policy
options.body: Restrict this PR to mismatched non-empty owners and track ownerless authority separately, leaving a known boundary ambiguity.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Confirm that plugins have no authority over ownerless rows and require deployed upgrade proof showing operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter's recent merged session lifecycle work touches the same handler and compatibility surface, making him the strongest available owner for the security-versus-upgrade policy choice.
